description: Nautilus is a framework that maps IP links to the submarine cables they probably traverse, so that the impact of cable failures on higher layers of the Internet can be studied. Using a corpus of public datasets and Internet cartographic techniques, it identifies IP links that likely cross submarine cables and assigns each to one or more potential cables with a prediction score reflecting confidence. It produces mappings for 3.05 million IPv4 links and 1.43 million IPv6 links covering 91% of all active cables. Without ground truth, the authors validate it by analysing past cable failures, running targeted traceroute measurements, and comparing with public network maps of two operators. Producer: Alagappan Ramanathan and Sangeetha Abdu Jyothi, version 4 dated 6 November 2023. Coverage: global submarine cable system. Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract page was read, so the code and mapping release, if any, were not confirmed. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: the mapping is a probabilistic inference validated indirectly. Simulation uses: the link-to-cable mapping lets network-flow and cascading-failure models estimate connectivity loss when a cable fails. Related records: the TeleGeography submarine cable map (data-telegeography-submarine-cable-map) and the solar superstorms robustness paper (model-solar-superstorms-internet-robustness-submarine-cables-sigcomm-2021).
